column1: # runs, one row per (run, case) pair, for R3.6/R3.7: neither a re-baseline nor
# a tightened gate margin should rest on a single sample or a single session.
# Columns: date (UTC, run generation time) / case / metric / pcrec value
# (throughput MB/s or latency ns/call) / within-run trial spread (max/min
# across BENCH_TRIALS, "n/a" if the run predates the spread column) / 1-min
# load average AT MEASUREMENT TIME (all rows below are quiet: well under the
# LOAD_LIMIT that run used) / source (results file or how the row was taken).
# Append rows here with `bash tests/bench/compare/rebaseline.sh` (see that
# script's header) rather than by hand, so provenance stays honest. A case
# needs several independent rows — taken in different sessions/times, not
# just several trials in one script invocation — before either a floors.tsv
# value (R3.6) or a compare-gate margin (R3.7) should be derived from it; see
# rebaseline.sh's REBASELINE_MIN_RUNS / gate.sh's EARN mode for the count each
# actually requires before it will act.
